source.label: theorem:regret-1d
source.quote: Suppose Algorithm~\ref{alg:1d} is run on a convex, 1-Lipschitz function $f$ bounded in [0,1]. Suppose the noise in observations is i.i.d. and $\sigma$-subgaussian. Then with probability at least $1 - 1/T$ we have \sum_{t=1}^T f(x_t) - f(x^*) \leq 108\sqrt{\sigma T\log T} \log_{4/3}\left(\frac{T}{8\sigma\log T}\right).

results.notes: Holds with probability at least 1-1/T (delta = 1/T fixed). Regret through f values (means). Known T; doubling mentioned in remarks.

symbols.c_1: algorithm constant: inner ball radius r = R/(c_1 d)
symbols.c_2: algorithm constant: pyramid apex angle with cos(phi) = c_2/d

conditions: f convex and 1-Lipschitz on compact convex X subset R^d

source.label: thm:highd
source.quote: Suppose Algorithm~\ref{alg:highd} is run with $c_1 \geq 64$, $c_2 \leq 1/32$ and parameters ... Then with probability at least $1-1/T$, the net regret incurred by the algorithm is bounded by 768d^3\sigma\sqrt{T}\log^2 T (\frac{2d^2\log d}{c_2^2} + 1)(\frac{4d^7c_1}{c_2^3} + \frac{d(d+1)}{c_2}) (\frac{4c_1 d^4}{c_2^2} + 11).

results.notes: Expression copied as stated in the theorem (constants in the proof differ slightly, e.g. d(d+2) and 12c_1). Holds w.p. >= 1-1/T. Computation analogous to ellipsoid method, described as efficient.
